Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 1:

Surat al-Jinn [Meccan, and its verses are twenty-eight]

﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, to the people: ﴿It has been revealed to me﴾, meaning I have been informed by revelation from God, Exalted is He, ﴿that it﴾ (the pronoun refers to the matter/affair), ﴿a group of the jinn listened﴾ to my recitation. They were jinn of Nasibin, and that was at the dawn prayer in Batn Nakhl, a place between Mecca and Ta'if. They are the ones mentioned in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We turned towards you a group of the jinn﴾ (Qur'an 46:29), and so on. ﴿They said﴾ to their people when they returned to them: ﴿Indeed we have heard a Qur'an, wondrous﴾, something to be marvelled at for its eloquence, the abundance of its meanings, and other than that.
﴿Yahdi ilā al-rushd﴾ (He guides to righteousness), i.e., faith and what is correct. ﴿So we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone﴾ with Him after today.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 3:

﴿And indeed He﴾: the pronoun refers to the matter (al-sha'n) here, and in this and the two following places. ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: He is exalted above, and far beyond, what has been attributed to Him in His majesty and greatness. ﴿He has not taken a companion﴾: a wife.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 4:

﴿Our foolish one﴾ (safīhunā), i.e., our ignorant one, ﴿spoke about Allah an outrageous lie﴾ (shaṭaṭan), i.e., they exceeded the bounds in falsehood by attributing to Him a consort and a son.

﴿And indeed we thought that﴾ is the lightened form (*mukhaffafa*), meaning that it (the subject) ﴿mankind and the jinn would never speak a lie against Allah﴾ by ascribing that to Him, until we realized their lie in that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 6:

﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn﴾ — they sought refuge (yasta'idhun) ﴿with men from the jinn﴾ when they halted during their journey in a frightening place, and each man would say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this place from the evil of its foolish ones." ﴿But they increased them﴾ — by their seeking refuge with them ﴿in burden (rahaqan)﴾, so they said: "We have become lords of the jinn and of mankind."

﴿And that they﴾ i.e., the jinn, ﴿thought as you thought﴾ O humankind, ﴿that﴾ أنْ (a mukhaffafa, the lightened form of the heavy particle, i.e., أنَّ) ﴿Allah will not resurrect anyone﴾ after his death.

The Jinn said: "And we touched the heaven, and found it filled with strong guards and blazing flames." (Qur'an 72:8) — we sought to eavesdrop, "and found it filled with" guards of the angels, "strong," and "flaming meteors," burning stars. This occurred when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent.

And we used to sit in some of its places to listen, [but] whoever listens now will find a watching flame lying in wait for him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: "And that we used to sit in it" — i.e., before his mission (ﷺ) — "places for listening", i.e., we would listen. "But whoever listens now will find for himself a watching flame" — it has been set in wait for him, so that it may be hurled at him.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 10:**

﴿And that we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth, or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾, after the eavesdropping, meaning good (khayran).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 11:

﴿And among us are the righteous﴾ after hearing the Qur'an, ﴿and among us are those who are other than that﴾, i.e., people who are not righteous, ﴿we were paths, divided sects﴾, groups differing from one another, Muslims and disbelievers.

Qur'anic quotations are in ﴿ ﴾ markers. Translate.

﴿And that we thought that﴾ is the lightened form of the heavy (anna), meaning that ﴿we will never escape Allah on the earth, nor will we escape Him by fleeing﴾, that is, we will not outpace Him whether we are on the earth or fleeing from it to the sky.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 13:

﴿And when we heard the guidance﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿we believed in it. Whoever believes in his Lord, then he does not fear﴾ with the supposed pronoun, i.e., he (fa-la yakhaf huwa), ﴿any diminution﴾ a reduction from his good deeds ﴿nor any oppression﴾ injustice by adding to his bad deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 14:

﴿And among us are the Muslims, and among us are the qāsitūn (those who deviate, the unjust) by their disbelief﴾ ﴿So whoever submits, those have sought out a right course﴾ (they intended guidance).

**"And as for the deviators, they have become fuel for Hell"**: *wuqudan* (fuel).

The *anna* forms (وأنا, وأنهم, وأنه) occur in twelve places in the surah, namely: وأنه فِي اثْنَيْ عَشَر مَوْضِعًا [and the cases in which *wa-annahu* appears], هِيَ [*hiya*], وأَنَّهُ تَعالى [*wa-annahu ta'ala*], وأَنّا مِنّا المُسْلِمُونَ [*wa-anna minna al-muslimun*], and what lies between them. The hamza in these words is read with a kasra (bi-kasr al-hamza) as a *istinaf* (a resumptive construction that begins a new clause, the term here glossing the idea of a fresh sentence), and with a fatha (bi-fathiha) as a grammatical construction, explained by what follows (bi-ma yuwajjah bihi).

And [that] (ﷺ) — no, correcting: this is not to be altered. Here is the translation:

"And" (wa-anna) is a lightened form of the heavy (anna), and its noun is omitted, meaning "and that they"; and it is conjoined to "that he listened" (annahu istama'a). ﴿If they had remained steadfast upon the Way﴾, meaning the way of Islam, ﴿We would surely have given them abundant water to drink﴾, plentiful, from the sky. This was after rain had been withheld from them for seven years.

﴿That We may test them therein﴾: that We may test them, so that We may know, with ʿilm ẓuhūr (knowledge of manifestation, i.e., knowledge as it becomes observable), how grateful they are. ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord﴾: the Qur'an. ﴿He will cause him to enter﴾: with the nūn or the yāʾ (both readings), We will admit him into ﴿a punishment, arduous﴾: difficult.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 18:

﴿And that the mosques﴾ are the places of prayer ﴿belong to God, so do not invoke﴾ within them ﴿anyone alongside God﴾ by associating [anyone with Him], as the Jews and Christians used to do: when they entered their synagogues and churches, they associated [others with God].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 19:

﴿And that﴾ (with fath and kasr, as a new sentence; the pronoun refers to the matter/affair), ﴿when the servant of Allah﴾ Muhammad the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿stood up, calling upon Him﴾ worshipping Him, ﴿in a hollow of palm trees﴾, ﴿they nearly became around him a mass﴾ meaning the jinn who were listening to his recitation. ﴿Layada﴾ (with kasr and damma on the lam) is the plural of lubdah, like lubad, from the jinn riding one another in crowds, eager to hear the Qur'an.
He said, answering the disbelievers in their saying "Return from what you are upon," and in another reading "Say": ﴿I only call upon my Lord﴾ as God,

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 21:

﴿Say, "Indeed, I do not possess for you [the power to cause] harm"﴾ [meaning] misguidance, ﴿or [for] guidance"﴾ [meaning] good.

Qur'an 72:22 is quoted with its meaning inside the ﴿ ﴾ markers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 22:

﴿Say: "Indeed, no one will protect me from Allah, and I will not find any refuge other than Him."﴾ [Meaning: from His punishment, if I disobey Him] ﴿no one will protect me from Allah [i.e., no one will protect me from Allah's punishment if I disobey Him]﴾ ﴿and I will not find any refuge other than Him﴾ [i.e., other than Him] ﴿a refuge﴾ [i.e., a place of shelter]

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 23:

﴿Except a notification﴾ is an exception from the object of (the verb) amlik (I possess/control), meaning: I do not possess for you anything except the notification to you ﴿from Allah﴾, i.e., from Him, ﴿and His messages﴾ is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to "notification," and what lies between the excepted element and the exception is a parenthetical insertion (iʿtirāḍ) for emphasizing the negation of capability. ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ in tawhid, so he does not believe, ﴿for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "man" (whoever), taking into account its meaning; and it is a predicated circumstance (ḥāl muqaddarah), and the meaning is that they will enter it for the duration of their abiding.

Surah 72, verse 24: "Until, when they see what they are promised, then they will know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti):

﴿Ḥattā idhā raʾaw﴾ is an initial (ibtidā'iyyah) particle (ḥattā, "until") which carries the sense of a limit (al-ghāyah) for an implied element before it, meaning: they will not cease in their disbelief until they see ﴿what they are promised﴾, namely the punishment with which they are threatened. ﴿Then they will know﴾ when it descends upon them, on the Day of Badr or on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number﴾, i.e., in aides: they or the believers? According to the first view, or I [i.e., the believers] or they, according to the second. Some of them said: "When is this promise?"

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 72, verse 25:

﴿Say: "I do not know﴾ i.e., I do not know ﴿whether what you are promised [of punishment] is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a term (amad)﴾, meaning a limit and an appointed time, which none knows except Him."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 72, verse 26:

﴿He is the Knower of the unseen﴾, [meaning] what is hidden from the servants. ﴿So He does not disclose﴾, i.e., does not inform ﴿of His unseen [knowledge] anyone﴾ from among the people.

Except for a messenger whom He has chosen; then indeed He makes a guard march before him and behind him, [while He also lets him know of what He wills, as a miracle for him]. ﴿Yasluku﴾ means He makes [it] go, or travels; ﴿from between his hands﴾, that is, the Messenger's; ﴿and from behind him a watch﴾, angels who guard him until he conveys it along with the rest of the revelation.

ﷻ

﴿لِيَعْلَم﴾ (so that He may know) — Allah's knowledge here is knowledge of manifestation (ʿilm ẓuhūr), i.e., that it becomes visible and actual. ﴿أنْ﴾ (that) is a lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy particle (al-thaqīlah), meaning: ﴿قَدْ أُبْلِغُوا﴾ (they have indeed conveyed), i.e., the messengers, ﴿رِسالات رَبّهمْ﴾ (the messages of their Lord). The pronoun is made plural in agreement with the meaning (ruʿiya bi-jamʿ al-ḍamīr maʿnā) by the phrase "min" (from). ﴿وأَحاطَ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ (and He encompasses what is with them) is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to an implied element, meaning: so He knew that. ﴿وأَحْصى كُلّ شَيْء عَدَدًا﴾ (and has enumerated everything in number) — "ʿadadan" is a specification (tamyīz), and it is transferred (muḥawwal) from the object; the original is: "aḥṣā ʿadad kull shayʾ" (He has counted the number of every thing).
